column1: # WHAT BIOME'S RULE DOMAINS ARE, and which of them a repository may claim.
# biome groups framework and library rules into DOMAINS. Under the org's
# `preset: "all"` every domain's rules are on regardless of what the repo
# is — measured on monumental-archive at #695: a React tree drew ten
# `useQwikValidLexicalScope` findings, a Qwik rule judging a React
# component. Declaring `domains: {react: "all"}` changes nothing
# (2164 diagnostics before and after, identical histogram); only the
# NEGATIVE has an effect (`qwik: "none"` → 2154, the ten gone). So the
# belt writes "none" for every identity domain a repo did not claim, and
# a repo never writes "none" itself. It states what it IS; the belt does
# the arithmetic. That is the whole reason this file exists.
# Columns, tab-separated: domain, kind, representative rule, and — for
# identity rows only — the comma-separated trigger packages. An org row
# stops at three columns rather than carrying an empty fourth, because a
# line ending in a tab is trailing whitespace and `lint:editorconfig`
# is right about that.
# EVERY VALUE IS DERIVED FROM `biome explain`, never authored here.
# `lint:biome-domains` re-derives it against the pinned binary in the
# canon's own gate — 14 explain calls, ~0.7s — so a renamed rule or a
# changed trigger reddens rather than rotting. `audit:biome-rules` holds
# the domain LIST against the pinned version's published schema, which
# is the network half and catches biome growing a fifteenth domain.
# KIND is the one adjudicated column. `project` and `types` are org
# strictness on biome's own metadata: neither has a dependency trigger at
# all, so neither is a statement about what a repo is — `types` is the
# seventeen type-aware rules and `project` the cross-file ones, which is
# the org's level, not the repo's shape.
# `test` IS triggered by a dependency (jest, mocha, ava, vitest) and is
# still org-fixed, which is the one row that needs an argument rather
# than a citation. Every repo in the org tests, and a repo testing under
# `node:test` declares no runner package at all — making `test` claimable
# would hand that repo a way to have no test rules and look conformant.
# Test-domain rules only fire on test-shaped code, so holding them at
# "all" everywhere costs a repo without tests exactly nothing.
# The other eleven are identity: each is auto-enabled by a dependency the
# repo either has or does not have, which is precisely the fact the belt
# cannot invent.
# A repo may claim a domain it has no dependency for: that turns rules ON
# and the hazard is one-directional, the lint:python-target shape. The
# reverse — having the dependency and not claiming it — is lowering an
# org rule by omission, and `lint:biome` refuses it.
